about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one.
title: Military conquest ideation round 2

messages.text: Read docs/design/DESIGNER-BRIEF.md and follow it — you are my game designer and co-ideation partner, stage 1 and 2 only. Round 1 is closed. Open round 2, military conquest, per docs/design/IDEATION-PLAN.md. Its inbox is docs/design/conquest-ideation.md.

One thing to note - on a high level this isn't a war game so your reasoning so far is accurate. I don't want this to be a game of just war and conquering and economics and diplomacy help your war effort. I want the game to be a game where war impacts your economy and diplomacy and internal relations and they all interact. 

As far as what that is/means - I agree that it is a standing state that will impact the state's relations with other countries.

I think that there needs to be other states as well which would be:

* War
* Cease-fire
* Hostile
* Peace-treaty
* Peace
* Subject
* Allied


We can get to the subject and allied later but the states would go as follows:

* Peace: you can do anything with the nation
* Peace-treaty: You signed a treaty with stipulations (trade, territory, repayment, etc) - breaking this will have a huge impact
* Hostile: Hostile relations happen when things happen between countries that bring them close to war but aren't at war. This will have impacts on things
* Cease-fire: All of the impacts of war but you cannot attack the other country
* War: Trade is prohibited and you are able to attack. (there might be some other stiupluations here)

Cease-fire is something that can only be a temporary state set for a set amount of turns.

What puts two nations as hostile would be a few things:

* One nation has a large growing movement in the other state (example - oregon is hostile with greater Idaho becasue the greater idaho movement is growing in their state.
* States are competing to reunify the same thing (texas/california/nyc and phillidalphia and washington DC and any other I am forgeting)
* If one nation is desperate for resrouces and the other won't trade for them or changes them an absurdly high price
* If one nation funds another movement in another nation
* If a nation a is allied to nation b and nation c is allied to nation d and nation a attacks nation c and d, nation d will be hostile with nation b.
* Anything else you mighjt suggest
I agree - I think down the road I could see a more complex version of the game being different but for now they are shared.

If houston is at war and it wants out of it and dallas refuses then they are still at war. I think at the end of the cease-fire agreement you can either default to three states war, peace-treaty, or hostile. After a peace-treaty you default back to peace. After a certain time hostile shoudl turn back to peace]

In my mind it will be similair to real life, at the end of a cease fire there will be a peace treay signed, or war will break out, or things will remain hostile. So at the end of a cease fire there should be a question if you want to send them a peace treaty. If no peace treaty is signed then things remain hostile. If a peace treaty is sent they should be able to send a counter offer and the cease fire would extend
Tolls rise, willingness to accept tolls rise, increases the growth of movements if they are apart of the matching state, increased cost of military guarding the border

Agreed - and another thing about war is that I want it to be really simple from a user experience level. There isn't going to be troops/troop types/etc.

My thought is that I decide I want to invade/annex an area. It would create a number of my total avaiable military for the field and compare it against the other nations set aside for the borter. There would be bonuses and negatives that will be decidd later on (like good tech increases your chance) or if you are annexing an area that is apart of your sepratist movement then that is a bonus as well. We can figure out the exact things later. 

I do like the idea of a percentage chance - it feels like your generals analyzed the data and are giving you a chance to win/succeed.

Lets do it like this. 

Dice rolls I take the area and it shows as my territory but with a different brightness of my map color and that area gets the modifier "occupied-war"

With that modifier it will increase civil unrest and impact the economy greatly. 

One main thing is that I will be able to use that as part of my trading but I cannot grant that as a toll to other countries as a trade passage. The logic is that even if I captured territory my allies wouldn't use it as as trade route while still at war. 

When a peace treaty is signed and if I keep that area it loses that modifier and gets "occupied" which will allow for all trade but still have some negative outcomes. 

The only other one we want to add is the modifier "occupied-movement" and in this one this is when a movement is more than 50% and is occupied by its matching movement.

I think mapping this onto a realistic outcome there are two options:

* concquer
* fails to conquer


Which means if they don't conquer it they have paid the cost and that was their turn and didn't conquer anything

Territory, repayment which cannot be more than 1.25 the cost of what they spent on war, forced trade deals, and how long it runs. If they say no then the war continues which will increase war weariness and increase chances of bad things happening.

I agree and there should be a new game mechanic that displays the movements demands (as well as their strength and support and any other info we decide later). 

So they might say something like start a war with this country. In each of these demands you can do one of three options:

* Implement it
* Decline to implement it
* Tell them to wait (which they will do but if you never implement it that will make them more angry than if you just declined in the first place)
Run sign-off and commit/push anything to github you need to and give me the prompt to start the next session with
